findings.claim: Guard hole: the production watchdog wiring in createInterface (chat_panel.py:269-272 - parent, setSingleShot, setInterval, timeout.connect) is exercised by no committed test. Layer 1 hand-injects a MagicMock timer; Layer 2 rebuilds its own QTimer in _wire_real_watchdog. Mutations W-M6 (connect line deleted), W-M7 (repeating timer), W-M8 (1 ms interval) survive under CPython and under hython 22.0.400. The crucible's probe builds the real interface offscreen and fires the production timer: wiring is correct today (single-shot, 35000 ms == WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS, not armed until a send, fires into _on_response_timeout, stays inactive after firing); its negative control with the connect line deleted reports fired=true, waiting_cleared=false, 0 lines - the probe catches W-M6 where the suite does not.

Evidence provenance: the receipt's rows 0-1 cite an 'offscreen hython real-QTimer probe (RESULT ALL PASS)' whose script is not on the branch (git diff --stat 79dbbfd9 c194d8a2 = product file, test file, receipt). The claim is true - the crucible re-established it through .synapse/hytest.py pinned to 22.0.400 (7 passed) - but it was not reproducible from the branch alone.

Guard hole: T-M6 (drop timeout=_t2 from the tier-2 guarded_create kwargs) survives - both fakes in tests/test_bp8_timeouts.py accept and ignore **kwargs, so nothing pins that the tier timeout reaches guarded_create and therefore the SDK (model_access.py:600). That kwarg is the row-4 mechanism and the load-bearing half of the receipt's finding 3 (abandoned workers bounded at the tier deadline); without it abandoned workers on the 4-worker _llm_pool run to the client-level 60 s ceiling (model_access.py:650) with a green suite.

Guard hole: T-M7 (drop _record_metric(RoutingTier.STANDARD, ..., False) from the tier-2 timeout branch) survives - target T1's clause 'record the metric as a failure for that tier' is untested on the timeout path (the tier-3 branch by construction likewise).

The handler's off-thread safety comment states a false premise for a true conclusion. It says route() 'touches no hou.* API'; route() reaches SynapseMemory.search, which is @_on_memory_main (store.py:1758-1759) and marshals through _read_on_main -> run_on_main whenever hou is present (store.py:1326-1341, :1218-1241), via enrich_context(memory=self._memory) (router.py:689-693 -> context_enrichment.py:82) and KnowledgeIndex._match_memory (knowledge.py:818); the memory passed is the real owner (handlers.py:1875). The offload is safe for a reason the comment does not name: route_chat is in _READ_ONLY_COMMANDS (handlers.py:237) and the websockets.sync server (websocket.py:365-380) calls handler.handle() directly on the per-client thread (websocket.py:566, :695-700), so the handler never runs on Houdini's main thread and a worker-to-main marshal behaves the same from the client thread and from _route_pool. The '28 s sits just under the 30 s slow-op kill' premise is also off: the read-only fast path has no per-command kill (websocket.py:700 has no timeout); the 30 s is run_on_main's _SLOW_TIMEOUT (main_thread.py:22) for hou marshals inside handlers. Before the leg a hung route() blocked that client's server thread with no bound; 28 s is a new ceiling by design. If route_chat were ever dispatched on the main thread, this offload would stall each memory-enriched turn until run_on_main's 10 s timeout and count toward is_main_thread_stalled(). Behaviour today unaffected; documentation nit with a sharp edge.
